item.text:
Reused evidence
No reusable item from the earlier chapter dossiers fits Chapter 4B cleanly, so this pass uses only new 2022-targeted evidence.

New evidence
- Electoral handover, Punjab
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"PM congratulates Shri Bhagwant Mann on taking oath as Punjab CM","publisher":"Prime Minister of India","publication_date":"2022-03-16","url":"https://www.pmindia.gov.in/en/news_updates/pm-congratulates-shri-bhagwant-mann-on-taking-oath-as-punjab-cm/","claim":"Modi congratulated AAP leader Bhagwant Mann after he took oath as Punjab chief minister and said the Centre would work with his government for Punjab's growth and welfare.","locator":"lines 73-80","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Official PMO page reproducing Modi's own tweet and public statement.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Direct 2022 state-election transfer within the target year.","ruler_attribution":"Directly attributable to Narendra Modi as prime minister and BJP leader.","contrary_evidence":["This is one congratulatory gesture; it does not by itself prove broader electoral fairness or institutional restraint."],"lenses":["4B.1","4B.8"]}

- Electoral handover, Himachal
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"PM congratulates Shri Sukhwinder Singh Sukhu on taking oath as Himachal Pradesh CM","publisher":"Prime Minister of India","publication_date":"2022-12-11","url":"https://www.pmindia.gov.in/en/news_updates/pm-congratulates-shri-sukhwinder-singh-sukhu-on-taking-oath-as-himachal-pradesh-cm/?comment=disable","claim":"Modi congratulated Congress leader Sukhwinder Singh Sukhu after he took oath as Himachal Pradesh chief minister and assured all possible cooperation from the Centre.","locator":"search-result snippet / official tweet text","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Official PMO public statement; the search snippet reproduces the tweet text even though the page was not line-openable in this session.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Direct 2022 opposition transition in Himachal Pradesh.","ruler_attribution":"Directly attributable to Narendra Modi.","contrary_evidence":["Again, this is a post-election gesture rather than evidence of deeper institutional self-binding."],"lenses":["4B.1","4B.8"]}

- Constitutional succession
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"PM congratulates Smt. Droupadi Murmu on being elected President","publisher":"Press Information Bureau, Government of India","publication_date":"2022-07-21","url":"https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=1843621","claim":"Modi congratulated Droupadi Murmu on being elected President of India and described the moment as historic for a tribal community.","locator":"search-result snippet","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Official government release quoting the prime minister's public reaction to a constitutional election result.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Direct 2022 constitutional transfer event inside the target year.","ruler_attribution":"Directly attributable to Narendra Modi.","contrary_evidence":["This confirms acceptance of a constitutional outcome, but it is not the same as broader reform of democratic institutions."],"lenses":["4B.8","4B.1"]}

- Sedition restraint
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Explained: Why Supreme Court’s order virtually stalls operation of sedition law","publisher":"The Indian Express","publication_date":"2022-05-12","url":"https://indianexpress.com/article/explained/why-supreme-courts-order-virtually-stalls-operation-of-sedition-law-7912401/","claim":"The Supreme Court said it would be appropriate not to continue using the sedition provision while the government re-examined it and that pending cases should be kept in abeyance.","locator":"lines 76 and 100-109","source_type":"media/legal","source_confidence":"medium_high","source_confidence_reason":"Contemporaneous legal reporting on a Supreme Court interim order; strong for the court's action, but not a direct Modi statement.","final_evidence_use":"context","period_fit":"Target-year 2022 and directly relevant to the government's treatment of dissent.","ruler_attribution":"Indirect: this shows the judiciary constraining the government, not a Modi-initiated reform.","contrary_evidence":["The order implies prior or attempted use of sedition, but the article does not establish Modi's personal direction."],"lenses":["4B.3","4B.9"]}

- Content takedown pressure
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Twitter pursues review of Indian orders to take down content","publisher":"Reuters via Trust.org","publication_date":"2022-07-05","url":"https://news.trust.org/item/20220705143902-o6u1w","claim":"Twitter sought judicial review of Indian government content-removal orders that included accounts supportive of an independent Sikh state, posts about farmer protests, and tweets critical of the government's COVID-19 handling.","locator":"lines 63-66","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"medium_high","source_confidence_reason":"Reuters reporting on a live legal challenge with specific content categories and the government's takedown demands.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly within 2022.","ruler_attribution":"Directly tied to Indian authorities under Modi's government, though the article does not prove personal direction by Modi.","contrary_evidence":["The report describes a legal dispute, so the government's legal justification is not adjudicated here."],"lenses":["4B.2","4B.6","4B.9"]}

- Internet shutdowns
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Five years in a row: India is 2022’s biggest internet shutdowns offender","publisher":"Access Now","publication_date":"2023-02-28","url":"https://www.accessnow.org/press-release/keepiton-internet-shutdowns-2022-india/","claim":"India carried out at least 84 internet shutdowns in 2022, including at least 49 in Jammu and Kashmir, and the report says shutdowns were used during protests and other high-salience periods to assert control.","locator":"lines 246-252","source_type":"NGO","source_confidence":"medium_high","source_confidence_reason":"Access Now is the leading shutdown-tracking NGO; the report is retrospective but directly covers 2022 and gives quantified country totals.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Retrospective but squarely about 2022 shutdown practice.","ruler_attribution":"Shared attribution across central and state authorities; not all shutdowns are personally traceable to Modi.","contrary_evidence":["The report also notes transparency and accountability gaps in how shutdown orders are documented, which limits precise central attribution."],"lenses":["4B.2","4B.6","4B.9","4B.10"]}

- Media crackdown
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"India: Suppression of Free Speech, Minorities","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","publication_date":"2023-01-12","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2023/01/12/india-suppression-free-speech-minorities","claim":"HRW said Indian authorities intensified and broadened the crackdown on activist groups and the media in 2022 and used abusive and discriminatory policies to repress Muslims and other minorities.","locator":"lines 607-610","source_type":"NGO","source_confidence":"medium_high","source_confidence_reason":"High-quality annual rights reporting with a clear 2022 focus and direct statements about the BJP-led government.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Retrospective on 2022 but explicitly centered on that year.","ruler_attribution":"Directly tied to the BJP-led government under Modi, though the report aggregates central, state, and local conduct.","contrary_evidence":["This is an annual overview, not a case-by-case judicial finding."],"lenses":["4B.3","4B.6","4B.7","4B.9"]}

- Foreign correspondent pressure
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Foreign correspondents increasingly refused permits, visas, access in India","publisher":"Reporters Without Borders","publication_date":"2023-04-19","url":"https://rsf.org/en/foreign-correspondents-increasingly-refused-permits-visas-access-india","claim":"RSF said Indian authorities escalated retaliatory measures against foreign correspondents by denying access or permits, including a September 2022 refusal affecting Vanessa Dougnac's right to work.","locator":"lines 326-330","source_type":"NGO","source_confidence":"medium_high","source_confidence_reason":"RSF is a specialized press-freedom monitor and the page gives a concrete 2022 case plus broader pattern language.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly relevant to 2022 press conditions.","ruler_attribution":"Directed at the Indian administration under Modi, though the specific permit decisions are bureaucratic and not individually traced to him.","contrary_evidence":["One named case does not quantify the full scale of the pressure on all foreign correspondents."],"lenses":["4B.6","4B.9"]}

- Dissent and assembly
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"India: Persecution of minorities and shrinking space for dissent: Amnesty International: Submission to the 41st session of the UPR Working Group, November 2022","publisher":"Amnesty International","publication_date":"2022-04-21","url":"https://www.amnesty.org/en/documents/asa20/5491/2022/en/","claim":"Amnesty said laws amended in India threatened freedom of expression and peaceful assembly and discriminated against Muslims and LGBTI people, while also raising concerns about religious violence and arbitrary deprivation of nationality.","locator":"lines 68-69","source_type":"NGO","source_confidence":"medium_high","source_confidence_reason":"Detailed country submission for the 2022 UPR cycle, with explicit rights claims and period fit.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Prepared for the 2022 UPR and describing the Modi period.","ruler_attribution":"Attributable to the Modi-era legal and policy environment, though not every measure began in 2022.","contrary_evidence":["It is an advocacy submission, not an adjudicated finding."],"lenses":["4B.3","4B.6","4B.7","4B.9"]}

- Religious intolerance
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Anti-Conversion Laws and Growing Intolerance in India","publisher":"United States Commission on International Religious Freedom","publication_date":"2022-05-06","url":"https://www.uscirf.gov/news-room/uscirf-spotlight/anti-conversion-laws-and-growing-intolerance-india","claim":"USCIRF said the Indian government promoted Hindu nationalism and facilitated systematic, ongoing, egregious violations of religious freedom, making the environment hostile to many non-Hindu communities.","locator":"lines 99-100","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"medium_high","source_confidence_reason":"USCIRF is a U.S. government commission; the statement is policy-oriented but directly tied to the Indian government's conduct.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"2022 source about the Modi period and the religious-freedom environment.","ruler_attribution":"Directly directed at the Indian government under Modi, though it is a broader rights assessment rather than a case finding.","contrary_evidence":["This is an evaluative commission statement, not a judicial determination of individual incidents."],"lenses":["4B.7","4B.3"]}

- Anti-minority violence and punitive demolitions
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"2022 Report on International Religious Freedom: India","publisher":"U.S. Department of State","publication_date":"2023-03-15","url":"https://www.ecoi.net/de/dokument/2091881.html","claim":"The report says police publicly flogged four Muslim men in Gujarat and that the Madhya Pradesh government bulldozed Muslim-owned homes and shops after communal violence, with UN rapporteurs calling the demolitions punitive.","locator":"lines 36-37 and 258","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Official U.S. government report summarizing documented 2022 incidents and citing UN rapporteurs and media corroboration.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly covers 2022 conduct.","ruler_attribution":"Primarily state and local attribution, with indirect responsibility at the Modi-led federal level through the political environment and tolerance of allied actors.","contrary_evidence":["Much of the conduct is at state or local level, so federal command is indirect rather than proven."],"lenses":["4B.7","4B.9"]}

- Damage-control after communal backlash
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"India's ruling party asks officials to exercise caution on religious issues after Islamic nations protest","publisher":"Reuters via Investing.com","publication_date":"2022-06-07","url":"https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/indias-ruling-party-asks-officials-to-exercise-caution-on-religious-issues-after-islamic-nations-protest-2834432","claim":"Reuters reported that BJP leaders told officials to be extremely cautious about religion on public platforms after derogatory remarks about the Prophet Mohammed drew protests from Islamic nations.","locator":"search-result snippet","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"medium_high","source_confidence_reason":"Reuters reporting, but accessed via a syndication host and only available here as a search snippet in this session.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly within 2022 and tied to a communal-political crisis.","ruler_attribution":"Attributed to the ruling party environment under Modi, though not to Modi's personal words.","contrary_evidence":["The warning followed inflammatory remarks and unrest, so it is damage control rather than evidence of prior restraint."],"lenses":["4B.3","4B.7","4B.10"]}

- Politicized investigations
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"The CBI Casebook: A surge in share of Opposition leaders in agency net","publisher":"The Indian Express","publication_date":"2022-09-20","url":"https://indianexpress.com/article/express-exclusive/from-60-per-cent-in-upa-to-95-per-cent-in-nda-a-surge-in-share-of-opposition-leaders-in-cbi-net-express-investigation-8160912/","claim":"An Indian Express investigation found that under BJP-led NDA-II, 118 of 124 prominent leaders facing CBI probes were from the opposition, and the agency had a reputation for acting at the behest of the Centre.","locator":"lines 20 and 45-46","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"medium","source_confidence_reason":"Investigative reporting based on court records, official documents, agency statements, and prior reports; strong as pattern evidence but still journalistic.","final_evidence_use":"context","period_fit":"Published in 2022 and summarizing the Modi-period investigative environment.","ruler_attribution":"Directed at the BJP-led central government, but the finding is a pattern claim rather than proof of direct Modi orders.","contrary_evidence":["The investigation spans multiple years, so it is not a pure 2022-only snapshot."],"lenses":["4B.2","4B.5"]}

Search and rejection summary
I reviewed roughly 30 documents and kept 13 distinct URLs. I rejected or collapsed:
- Duplicate coverage of the same incidents across Reuters, ReutersConnect, NDTV, India Today, Times of India, Hindustan Times, and The Economic Times when one stronger source already captured the material fact.
- Purely visual or caption-only ReutersConnect items because they added little beyond the text reports.
- Out-of-period pages from 2023-2026 that described later events rather than 2022 conditions.
- General country-profile material that repeated the local structured priors without adding ruler-specific attribution.
- Broad opinion pieces and advocacy pages when a stronger official, court, or investigative source was available for the same point.
- Evidence about national security, international diplomacy, or domestic crime that did not bear directly on political freedom.
- Several election-adjacent items from the Election Commission and PIB that were useful background but not as strong as the direct Modi congratulatory messages for contestability and transfer.
- Later press-freedom summaries that duplicated HRW, RSF, Amnesty, or Access Now on the same 2022 media and digital-control pattern.

Remaining gaps
- 4B.4 is still thin: I did not find strong 2022 evidence that Modi personally strengthened independent courts, legislatures, audit bodies, or oversight institutions when they constrained him. The sedition order shows judicial constraint, not ruler self-binding.
- 4B.5 is only partly covered: I have good evidence for politicization of state agencies, but weaker direct evidence on personality cult mechanics, loyalty tests, or party capture specifically in 2022.
- 4B.1 is covered mainly through Modi's public acceptance of state-level opposition victories and a constitutional presidential election, not through deeper evidence on election administration integrity.
- More search would help if you want a denser record on central-vs-state attribution for internet shutdowns, media pressure, and punitive demolitions.
